sets.label: Cities on the fall line (Adult enthusiast, expert)

origin.author: READY builder
origin.source_reference: Original draft material; not an official assessment; awaiting owner review

connections.feedback: Land above the fall line is generally higher and more rolling. Flat building land was not the reason.
Rivers at the fall line are fresh water. The advantage was the end of navigation and the waterpower.
Correct. Falls and rapids ended river travel from the coast and powered mills, so goods changed hands and industry grew.
The fall line is a physical feature, not a political boundary. Towns grew there because of the river's drop.

origin.author: READY builder
origin.source_reference: Original draft material; not an official assessment; awaiting owner review

connections.feedback: No standard unit has that shape. A section is one mile by one mile.
That is a quarter section, one fourth of a standard section.
That is a township, which contains 36 sections.
Correct. A standard section is one mile on each side, which is 640 acres. A township has 36 of them.

sets.label: Why Alaska looks oversized (Adult enthusiast, advanced)

origin.author: READY builder
origin.source_reference: Original draft material; not an official assessment; awaiting owner review

connections.feedback: A flat map has no viewing distance. The oversizing comes from how the globe is flattened.
Mapmakers do not resize places by their roads. The size change comes from the projection's math.
Mercator does not shrink the equator by a fixed share. Its distortion grows steadily toward the poles.
Correct. Mercator keeps directions true but enlarges areas toward the poles, so far northern places look oversized.

origin.author: READY builder
origin.source_reference: Original draft material; not an official assessment; awaiting owner review

connections.feedback: Pilots do not add distance to burn fuel. The path is short on the globe, though it looks bent on a map.
Correct. A great-circle route is the shortest distance on the globe. Many flat maps show it as a curve.
No such rule exists. The route is curved because of how the globe is flattened onto a map.
Magnetic pull does not drag planes south. Their routes follow the shortest path and wind conditions.

sets.label: Great Lake wholly in the U.S. (Adult enthusiast, advanced)

origin.author: READY builder
origin.source_reference: Original draft material; not an official assessment; awaiting owner review

connections.feedback: Correct. Lake Michigan is the only Great Lake entirely inside the United States.
Lake Superior is shared with Canada, along its northern shore.
Lake Erie is shared with Canada, along its northern shore.
Lake Ontario is shared with Canada, along its northern shore.

sets.label: Largest Great Lake by area (Adult enthusiast, advanced)

origin.author: READY builder
origin.source_reference: Original draft material; not an official assessment; awaiting owner review

connections.feedback: Lake Michigan is large and well known, but Lake Superior is bigger.
Lake Huron is a very large lake, but its surface area is smaller than Lake Superior's.
Lake Erie is one of the smaller Great Lakes by area.
Correct. Lake Superior is the largest of the Great Lakes by surface area.

sets.label: Where the Niagara River ends (Adult enthusiast, advanced)

origin.author: READY builder
origin.source_reference: Original draft material; not an official assessment; awaiting owner review

connections.feedback: Correct. The Niagara River carries water from Lake Erie over the falls and into Lake Ontario.
Lake Erie is where the Niagara River begins, so the river flows out of it, not into it.
Lake Superior is the farthest upstream of the Great Lakes, not connected to the Niagara River.
Lake Huron is farther upstream in the Great Lakes chain and is not connected to the Niagara River directly.

sets.label: Arizona's clocks in summer (Adult enthusiast, expert)

origin.author: READY builder
origin.source_reference: Original draft material; not an official assessment; awaiting owner review

connections.feedback: In summer, Eastern daylight time is three hours ahead of Arizona's clocks, so it does not match.
Arizona is in the Mountain zone and stays on its standard time, so the name fits. But in summer the rest of the Mountain zone moves ahead one hour, so Arizona's clocks differ from theirs.
connections.notes: Zone name versus the clock actually shown. A reasonable reading of the stem, so ambiguous; the strong answer matches the clock difference.

connections.feedback: Correct. Arizona stays on Mountain standard time, which in summer matches Pacific daylight time.
In summer, Central daylight time is two hours ahead of Arizona's clocks, so it does not match.

sets.label: Time zone of the western Panhandle (Adult enthusiast, advanced)

origin.author: READY builder
origin.source_reference: Original draft material; not an official assessment; awaiting owner review

connections.feedback: Correct. Part of the western Panhandle is in the Central time zone. The rest of the state is Eastern.
The Mountain zone is much farther west. No part of Florida uses it.
Eastern time is used by most of Florida, so it is the zone the Panhandle's western end differs from.
The Pacific zone is on the West Coast. No part of Florida uses it.

sets.label: Cause of chinook winds (Adult enthusiast, advanced)

origin.author: READY builder
origin.source_reference: Original draft material; not an official assessment; awaiting owner review

connections.feedback: Correct. Air that sinks down a mountain's lee side warms as it is compressed. The result is a warm, dry wind.
Volcanic heat is not the cause. Descending, compressed air creates the warmth.
Rising air cools. Warming happens when air sinks down the far side of a mountain.
Ocean currents do not cross the Rockies. The warming happens as air descends the slope.

sets.label: Opposite sides of the Continental Divide (Adult enthusiast, expert)

origin.author: READY builder
origin.source_reference: Original draft material; not an official assessment; awaiting owner review

connections.feedback: Within the United States, the divide does not send water north to the Arctic on both sides.
Correct. The divide separates water flowing toward the Pacific from water flowing toward the Atlantic side. A few interior basins drain to neither.
The divide is a real ridge line. Water on each side flows to a different ocean basin.
The Great Basin is a separate region of interior drainage. It is not the destination of the water on both sides of the divide.

origin.author: READY builder
origin.source_reference: Original draft material; not an official assessment; awaiting owner review

connections.feedback: This is a real and common description of Missouri, so it is defensible. It does not give the Census placement, which the question expects.
connections.notes: Common cultural description, true as far as it goes, but it does not answer which region the Census Bureau assigns. Marked ambiguous.

connections.feedback: Correct. The official Census region is the Midwest, but many people find Southern ties in Missouri's history and culture.
The Census Bureau places Missouri in the Midwest. Some other sources place it in the South, but that is not the Census assignment.
Touching the Plains does not make a state part of the West. The Census Bureau places Missouri in the Midwest.

sets.label: Park with active volcanoes (Adult enthusiast, advanced)

origin.author: READY builder
origin.source_reference: Original draft material; not an official assessment; awaiting owner review

connections.feedback: Haleakala is a real volcanic park, but it is on the island of Maui, not on the island of Hawaii.
Crater Lake is a volcanic park in Oregon, on the mainland, not in Hawaii.
Correct. Hawaii Volcanoes National Park, on the island of Hawaii, protects Kilauea and Mauna Loa.
Carlsbad Caverns, in New Mexico, protects caves formed in rock, not volcanoes.

sets.label: River beside the Gateway Arch (Adult enthusiast, advanced)

origin.author: READY builder
origin.source_reference: Original draft material; not an official assessment; awaiting owner review

connections.feedback: The Missouri joins the Mississippi just north of St. Louis, but the arch stands beside the Mississippi.
The Ohio River meets the Mississippi far to the southeast, at the southern tip of Illinois.
Correct. The Gateway Arch stands on the west bank of the Mississippi, not far below the Missouri River's mouth.
The Colorado River flows through the Southwest, far from St. Louis.

origin.author: READY builder
origin.source_reference: Original draft material; not an official assessment; awaiting owner review

connections.feedback: Honolulu is the farthest south of the four and has the smallest summer change in daylight.
Phoenix is hot, but its daylight hours are shorter than at higher latitudes.
Correct. Daylight in summer lengthens with latitude. Anchorage is the farthest north of the four.
Miami is far south, so its June days are shorter than those in the far north.

origin.author: READY builder
origin.source_reference: Original draft material; not an official assessment; awaiting owner review

connections.feedback: Lake Superior is the westernmost of the five, not the easternmost.
Lake Erie is just west of Lake Ontario, so it is not the farthest east.
Lake Huron is farther west, upstream of Lake Erie.
Correct. Lake Ontario is the easternmost Great Lake, at the end of the chain.

sets.label: Time zone of northern Idaho (Adult enthusiast, advanced)

origin.author: READY builder
origin.source_reference: Original draft material; not an official assessment; awaiting owner review

connections.feedback: The Central zone is far to the east. No part of Idaho uses it.
Mountain time is what most of Idaho uses, so it is the zone the northern Panhandle differs from.
The Eastern zone is on the other side of the country. No part of Idaho uses it.
Correct. The northern Idaho Panhandle is on Pacific time, like neighboring Washington.
